title: CRLR/99/2011 of SURENDRA RAM Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ANR

paras.text:
CRLR No.98 of 2011
with
CRLR No. 99 of 2011
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Raj Kumar Singh Verma, Advocate
for the petitioner.
Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, Assistant
Government Advocate for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent no. 1.
Mr. I.P. Kohli, Advocate for respondent
no. 2.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Since common questions of fact and
law are involved in these revisions, therefore
both these revisions are clubbed together
and are being heard & decided together.
However, for the sake of convenience, facts
of CRLR No. 98 of 2011 are being
considered.
Revisionists in these Criminal Revisions
are Government Servants. Revisionist in
Criminal Revision No. 98 of 2011 was
serving as Additional District Magistrate;
while, revisionist in Criminal Revision No. 99
of 2011 was serving as Sub Divisional
Magistrate at Dehradun. A complaint case
was filed against the revisionists by one Mr.
Santlal (respondent no. 2 herein) alleging
that the revisionists' alongwith other
Government Officers visited the land
belonging to Santlal and forcibly
dispossessed him in order to handover
possession of the said land to Mr. Ram
Awtar and Mr. Dinesh Kumar. It is alleged in
the said complaint that the revisionists not
only misused their official position by filing
Challan against the complainant under
Section 107/116 Cr.P.C.; but, also
misbehaved with the complainant and his

family members and also caused bodily
injuries to them.
Learned Magistrate, after recording
statement of the complainant under Section
200 Cr.P.C. and statements of the witnesses
under Section 202 Cr.P.C., registered the
complaint as Complaint Case No. 1071 of
2003 for the offences punishable under
Sections 323, 504, 506 & 120-B I.P.C.
Learned Magistrate, after hearing the
parties, refused to frame charge against both
the revisionists vide order dated 27.03.2009
and directed for framing of charge only
against Mr. Ram Awatar. Mr. Santlal
(complainant), thereafter, filed a Criminal
Revision under Section 397 Cr.P.C., which
was registered as Criminal Revision No. 68
of 2009. Mr. Ram Awatar, against whom
learned Magistrate had directed for framing
of charge, also challenged the order passed
by learned Magistrate by filing Criminal
Revision No. 72 of 2009. Both these
Criminal Revisions were decided together by
a common judgment & order dated
05.04.2011 passed by learned Additional
District Judge/F.T.C.-6, Dehradun. The
Criminal Revision filed by Mr. Ram Awatar
was dismissed; while, Criminal Revision filed
by Mr. Santlal was partly allowed and the
order passed by learned Magistrate was
modified and it was provided that charge be
framed against the present revisionists also.
Thus, feeling aggrieved, Mr. Jitendra Singh
and Mr. Surendra Ram have filed these
Criminal Revisions under Section 397/401
Cr.P.C.
Heard learned counsel for the parties
and perused the record.
Learned counsel for the revisionists
submits that learned Revisional Court/

Additional District Judge erred in directing
learned Magistrate to frame charge against
revisionists, namely, Mr. Jitendra Singh and
Mr. Surendra Ram. He submits that learned
Additional District Judge exceeded powers
available to him under Section 397 & 398
Cr.P.C. He further submits that the
revisionists are Public Servants, who were
acting in terms of the order passed by High
Court, therefore, they are entitled to
protection under Chapter IV of I.P.C., more
particularly, under Sections 76, 78 & 79 of
I.P.C. He further submits that, being Public
Servants, revisionists are also entitled to
protection under Section 197 Cr.P.C. Thus,
according to him, learned Revisional Court
was not justified in ignoring this aspect of
the matter, which has resulted in
miscarriage of justice. He further submits
that the order passed by learned Revisional
Court is unsustainable in the eyes of law.
Per contra, learned counsel for the
complainant (respondent no. 2 herein)
submits that neither the revisionists are
entitled to protection of any provision
contained in Chapter IV of I.P.C. nor they
are entitled to protection under Section 197
Cr.P.C., inasmuch as, there was no order of
any Court directing the revisionists to put
Ram Awatar into possession of the land in
question. He further submits that there is no
nexus between the act committed by the
revisionists and their official duties and
whatever act was committed by the
revisionists was outside the scope of their
official duties.
Without going into merits of the rival
contention of parties, this Court finds that in
the absence of any compelling
circumstances, learned Revisional Court was

not justified in directing the learned
Magistrate to frame charges against the
present revisionists. Thus, on this short
point alone, these Criminal Revisions
deserve to be allowed.
In such view of the matter, the
Criminal Revisions are allowed. Impugned
order dated 05.04.2011 passed by learned
Revisional Court/Additional District Judge/
F.T.C.-6, Dehradun is set aside.
The matter is remitted back to the
learned Revisional Court to decide the
Criminal Revision filed by Mr. Santlal afresh,
in accordance with law, untrammeled by the
orders impugned in these Criminal
Revisions.
